user.title: MatterBook
user.description:
MatterBook keeps your Matter setup codes in `config/matterbook/` and commissions the devices it recognises when they turn up in pairing mode.

That folder holds device passcodes, so treat it like secrets.yaml.

data.require_exact_match: Only pair on an exact discriminator match
data.use_bluetooth: Also scan Home Assistant's Bluetooth advertisements
data.apply_metadata: Apply the stored name and area after pairing
data.max_attempts: Attempts before giving up on an entry
data.allow_trials: Allow one blind attempt per entry
data.pair_on_add: Try to pair straight after adding an entry

data_description.require_exact_match: A manual pairing code only carries 4 bits of discriminator, so one in sixteen devices matches by chance. Turn this on to act only on entries stored as a scanned QR payload.
data_description.use_bluetooth: Reads advertisements Home Assistant already collects, including those relayed by ESPHome Bluetooth proxies.
data_description.retry_cooldown: Doubles with every failed attempt, up to eight times this value.
data_description.allow_trials: An 8-digit setup passcode names no device at all, and a manual pairing code names one in sixteen. When exactly one entry and one device are left unaccounted for, MatterBook may spend a single attempt on it — once per entry, never repeatedly.
data_description.pair_on_add: The moment you type in a code is usually the moment the device is in front of you and blinking, and the moment the fewest other devices are in pairing mode.

add_entry.name: Add entry
add_entry.description: Adds a device to the MatterBook.

code.name: Setup code
code.description: The QR payload (MT:...), the 11- or 21-digit manual pairing code, or the bare 8-digit setup passcode. A QR payload is worth the most: it names exactly which device the code opens.

name.name: Name
name.description: Name to give the device once it is paired.

area.name: Area
area.description: Area to put the device in once it is paired.

notes.name: Notes
notes.description: Free-form note, such as where the device is.

serial_number.name: Serial number
serial_number.description: Serial number, for your own records.

remove_entry.name: Remove entry
remove_entry.description: Removes a device from the MatterBook.

row.name: Row
row.description: 1-based row number, as shown on the Entries sensor.

entry_id.name: Entry ID
entry_id.description: Stable id of the entry, which does not shift when other rows are deleted.

scan.name: Scan
scan.description: Scans for commissionable Matter devices and pairs the ones the book knows, if auto-pairing is on.

pair.name: Pair
pair.description: Commissions one MatterBook entry now, whether or not it was seen in a scan.

row.name: Row
row.description: 1-based row number, as shown on the Entries sensor.

reload_book.name: Reload book
reload_book.description: Re-reads the MatterBook file from disk, after editing it outside Home Assistant.

import_from_matter.name: Import from Matter
import_from_matter.description: Adds every device already commissioned onto this fabric to the MatterBook. Their setup codes cannot be imported — a commissioned device keeps a verifier, not its passcode — so each row records what the device is and where it lives, and waits for its sticker.

set_code.name: Set code
set_code.description: Gives an imported entry its setup code, once you have found the sticker.

code.name: Setup code
code.description: The QR payload (MT:...), manual pairing code, or 8-digit passcode.

replace.name: Replace
replace.description: Allow overwriting a code the entry already has.
